applied.problem: "Real trolleys also lose a little to their wheels' spin, to any slope" is off: a slope can speed a trolley up as well as slow it, and spinning wheels make it respond as if a little heavier rather than losing momentum.
"The trolley stops 10 s and 2.5 m later" holds only from the opening 0.5 m/s; at the 1 m/s top of the drag it takes 20 s and 10 m, so the figure must be tied to the opening speed.

"It needs one only to make up for friction" is too absolute for the dossier (uphill or into drag it needs more); "A force sets how fast the speed changes" should be the net force; 2000 N to stop in 0.5 s is the average force, not a fixed one.
"Real rolling resistance changes a little with speed and load" understates load: rolling resistance grows roughly in proportion to the load, though only a little with speed.
"A coil has no twin of the third law" is absolute; two coupled coils do act on each other equally (mutual inductance is the same both ways), so the claim should be limited to a single coil.
